summary: Troyes is a dice-and-card worker placement game where your workers are dice whose rolled values determine what they can do, and you're constantly trading, selling, or losing dice to opponents and events. It's a tight economic engine game with a distinctive push-your-luck feel layered onto worker placement, since die values fluctuate and can be manipulated by cards.
praised: unique dice-as-workers mechanism that feels fresh even to experienced gamers
deep, tense economic engine-building with many viable strategies
strong replayability from variable card decks and interaction between religious/military/civic tracks
clever way of turning dice rolling into a strategic resource rather than pure luck
criticised: steep learning curve and dense rulebook that intimidates new players
significant luck from dice rolls, even if mitigated by manipulation options
downtime and analysis paralysis in higher player counts
can feel fiddly and overwrought with icons/tracks for newcomers

interaction.kind: worker/die trading, selling dice to opponents, and competing for limited action spaces

scoring.why: points come from multiple tracks (military, religious, civic influence) plus card bonuses, favoring balanced engine-building over one dominant strategy
